HOLDERS: only Vanguard Capital Management (5.3%, Schedule 13G filed April 30, 2026) is listed above 5%; the proxy gives the filing date, not the holding date, so asOf is null. BlackRock no longer appears in the table. BUYBACKS: the 2025 cash-flow statement has no share repurchase line, so 0. footprint.notes: Tesla publishes no state, country or regional breakdown of employees, stores, service centers or Supercharger sites in its FY2025 10-K or its quarterly Update decks; both give only global totals, so countries and regions are null. Sites are the eight primary manufacturing facilities in FY2025 10-K Item 2 (unchanged from the prior year) plus the Austin headquarters. Vehicle-factory capacity figures come from the newest quarterly Update deck, Q3 2026 (installed capacity, not production; Tesla's IR files moved from digitalassets.tesla.com to assets-ir.tesla.com). In Q3 2026 the California line shows only Model 3 / Model Y (>550,000; Model S / Model X no longer listed), Texas Model Y rose to >375,000 and Cybercab shows >125,000 in production; the deck also shows Tesla Semi at 25,000 in Nevada and Megafactory Texas beginning production, which are not added as sites. Gigafactory Shanghai and Megafactory Shanghai: Tesla owns the buildings and holds 50-year land use rights. The 'employees' metric (IHS Markit's 2018–2021 California study, commissioned by Tesla) has no rows: one state cannot make a state map and the figure is old; no newer Tesla state study was found (checked 2026-11-24). Tesla also hosts a 'Gigafactory Nevada Economic and Fiscal Impact Analysis 2022' (Applied Analysis), whose headcounts combine Tesla with on-site vendors and indirect and induced jobs, so no Tesla-only Nevada figure is recorded. Period: 10-K as of Dec 31, 2025; capacity as of Q3 2026.

ventures.notes: Tesla, the primary company, stays in research/lenses/marketcap. SpaceX listed on Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas in June 2026 (Class A only, symbol SPCX). It absorbed xAI, and with it X (formerly Twitter), on February 2, 2026, so X is counted inside SpaceX and not separately. The prospectus biography also names Zip2 Corporation, which he co-founded and which Compaq acquired in March 1999. Apart from Tesla and PayPal (already on the list), no other company in that biography is listed today. The founder wording for Neuralink and The Boring Company comes from SpaceX's prospectus, not from either company's own filing; both are private. The years are the incorporation years in each company's own Form D: Neuralink Corp. (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1708503/000170850317000001/xslFormDX01/primary_doc.xml, "Within Last Five Years (Specify Year) 2016") and TBC - The Boring Co (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1737630/000173763018000001/xslFormDX01/primary_doc.xml, "Within Last Five Years (Specify Year) 2017"). The prospectus gives no year for PayPal, so its year is null. Musk’s economic share of SpaceX is derived from the prospectus table (shares he owns outright ÷ all shares outstanding), because the prospectus states only class and voting percentages.
